name: IL-12
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Mike Bost running with large financial edge
Fortier's minimal fundraising (~$88K) and no outside support
Markets price Bost at ~96% to win
model.rationale: The district's R+22 lean, Bost's incumbency, and his roughly 15-to-1 fundraising advantage over Fortier leave no evidence pointing toward an upset, and prediction markets agree at about 96% Republican. The forecast stays essentially at the fundamentals-based baseline.
model.watch: Any late surge in Democratic outside spending or a polling surprise showing Bost under 55% would warrant a modest shift.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Southern Illinois' 12th District is firmly Republican territory, with a partisan lean of about 22 points toward the GOP. Incumbent Mike Bost is running for another term after easily securing his nomination, and he holds a commanding financial position with roughly $790,000 on hand. His Democratic challenger, Julie Fortier, has raised under $90,000 with no outside spending on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals, and those point decisively to Bost. Prediction markets price his reelection chances at about 96 percent. The environment could be somewhat better for Democrats than in past cycles, but a 20-plus-point structural gap leaves little realistic path for an upset here.
